00 · MiniMax-H3 — verified model facts
Source-audited 2026-10-27. Re-verify prices/limits before spending money: they change.
What H3 actually is
A general-purpose omni-modal generative system: text / image / video / audio in → video with native stereo audio out, up to 2K, 4–15 s, 24 fps, 32 kHz stereo.


Three modules exist; only one of them is downloadable:


Module
	What it does
	Open weights?
	H3-Context-IR
	Hosted prompt understanding / rewrite into a structured "context IR". MiniMax calls it critical to output quality.
	❌ API only
	H3-Base
	The actual generator (FL2VA + Ref2VA checkpoints).
	✅ open weights
	H3-Regenerate-2K
	Re-generates a 768p result into 2K using the original context (not a normal upscaler).
	❌ API only
	

So: local deployment = 768p only. 2K needs the hosted regeneration API (or the hosted 2K generation endpoint).
Two open checkpoints
Checkpoint
	Supported tasks
	Inputs
	MiniMax-H3 Base FL2VA
	t2va text-to-audio-video · fl2va first/last-frame-to-audio-video
	text + 0/1/2 keyframes
	MiniMax-H3 Base Ref2VA
	ref2va reference-to-audio-video
	text + ≤9 images, ≤3 videos (2–15 s each, ≤15 s total), ≤3 audio clips (2–15 s each) — max 12 files
	Architecture (why it is heavy)
Component
	Role
	BF16 weight size
	H3-Omni-Transformer
	33B dense single-stream DiT; jointly denoises video + audio latents. ~13B live in AdaLN branches that can be precomputed/cached for inference
	≈ 66 GB (≈ 40 GB after AdaLN caching / pruning)
	H3-Encoder
	full Qwen3-VL-32B, hidden states from layer 50
	≈ 51–62 GB
	H3-VisualVAE
	f16t4d24 (16× spatial, 4× temporal, 24 latent ch)
	≈ 10 GB
	H3-AudioVAE
	32 kHz stereo, 40 Hz latent rate, channel-independent
	≈ 0.6 GB
	Resident total
	

	≈ 100–128 GB
	

Full BF16 checkpoint release ≈ 124–144 GB on disk. That single number decides every deployment question: this model does not fit on one free Colab GPU, and does not fit in Colab at all in BF16.

	fits

Practical minimum for the official diffusers / SGLang path: a single 80 GB card with a pruned INT8 build (~42 GB working set), or multi-GPU for BF16.
Inference frameworks (official list)
* SGLang — sglang serve --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode speed --model-variant fl2va (port 30010) / ref2va (30011).
* vLLM — recipes at recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3.
* diffusers — ModularPipeline.from_pretrained("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3") (needs the minimax-h3 diffusers branch until it lands on PyPI; diffusers>=0.32.2 is the floor in requirements.txt).
* ComfyUI — official tutorial + video_minimax_h3_t2v.json / video_minimax_h3_r2v.json templates; Comfy-Org publishes a pruned INT8 workflow set (~42.5 GB).
Hosted API (the route that actually works from Colab)
Base URL: https://api.minimax.io (global) or https://api.minimaxi.com (CN). Auth: Authorization: Bearer <API key>.


Call
	Method + path
	Create video
	POST /v2/video_generation
	Query task
	GET /v2/query/video_generation/{task_id}
	Context-IR rewrite
	/video-generation-v2-h3-context-ir (see README of the H3 repo + platform docs)
	768P → 2K regeneration
	/video-generation-v2-regeneration
	

Model variants on the create endpoint:


Model
	Resolutions
	Duration
	Notes
	MiniMax-H3
	768P, 2K
	4–15 s
	t2v, i2v (first/last frame), reference-to-video
	MiniMax-H3-Highspeed
	768P
	4–15 s
	quality/speed balance, ref image/video/audio
	MiniMax-H3-Lite
	480P, 768P
	4–15 s
	cheapest, no adaptive ratio
	MiniMax-H3-Max
	480P, 768P
	5–15 s
	fastest, extra.prompt_expansion_mode only
	

Request shape (t2va):


{


  "model": "MiniMax-H3",


  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "<prompt>" }],


  "resolution": "2K",


  "duration": 5,


  "ratio": "16:9"


}


content[] items: text, image_url (role: first_frame / last_frame / reference_image), video_url (role: reference_video), audio_url (role: reference_audio). image-to-video and reference-to-video are mutually exclusive — you cannot mix first_frame with reference_image.


Limits: total body ≤ 64 MB (use public URLs, not base64, for large files); image ≤ 30 MB, side 256–5760 px, ratio 0.4–2.5, first/last frame ≤ 1 each, reference images ≤ 9; video ≤ 50 MB each, ≤ 3 clips, 2–15 s each and ≤ 15 s total, H.264/H.265 + AAC/MP3; audio WAV/MP3, ≤ 15 MB each, ≤ 3 clips, 2–15 s each and ≤ 15 s total. For t2va, ratio is required and may not be adaptive. For i2va, ratio is forced to adaptive.
Pricing (official pay-as-you-go, list)
Item
	Price
	MiniMax-H3 output @ 768P
	$0.08 / s
	MiniMax-H3 output @ 2K
	$0.13 / s
	MiniMax-H3-Highspeed @ 768P
	$0.06 / s
	MiniMax-H3-Lite @ 768P
	$0.04 / s
	MiniMax-H3-Max @ 480P / 768P
	$0.05 / $0.08 / s
	768P → 2K regeneration
	$0.05 / s
	Reference audio input
	free
	Reference images
	first 5 free, then $0.04 each
	Reference video input
	billed per input second at the output rate
	

Worked examples: 10 s @768P = $0.80; 10 s @2K = $1.30; 15 s @2K = $1.95; a 60 s finished film built from 6 × 10 s 2K shots = $7.80 plus retries.
Licence — read before publishing
The MiniMax H3 Community License (effective 2026-08-02) is not OSI open source. Its "Applicable Territory" excludes the United States, EU, United Kingdom and South Korea for local deployment without separate authorisation from MiniMax (application form in the repo). Hosted-API use is governed by the platform terms. This repository's default work (Pakistan) is outside the excluded territories, but any client delivery into those regions needs a rights note in the project record.
Honest risks
1. Guardrails: user text/images/videos and the enhanced prompt are moderated; error 1026 = "video description contains sensitive content" (HTTP 422). A blocked prompt still costs nothing but wastes a turn.
2. H3-Context-IR is hosted and closed. Writing prompts in its structure yourself (see 02_PROMPTING.md) is the only portable substitute, and it changes output quality materially.
3. 2K from local weights is impossible; do not promise 2K to a client from a local/ComfyUI run.
4. Identity drift: reference-to-video keeps a face recognisable but not pixel-identical across shots. Cast-level consistency needs one locked reference set and the same seed-free prompt skeleton per shot.
